newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- US T-bonds hesitate at channel resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- US T-bonds hesitate at channel resistance.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures are looking hesitant near the top of a two-month-old rising channel, although their upward momentum is still intact, technical analysts said.
For September futures, that channel resistance came in at the 112-area, where the market topped out Friday and so far today, said Terence Gabriel, an analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc.
"We're dealing basically with the upper channel and Friday's probe (of 112-2/32 high)," he said. "We may need to regroup a bit before we get a decisive penetration of those levels."
With the 61.8-percent Fibonacci retracement of the December-April decline at 111-28/32, the 112-area could be a very "sticky" level for now, he added.
Still, he noted that trend-strength indicators like the ADX or the Bollinger band width were still rising, showing that the upward momentum was still building.
Matthew Crosson, director of fixed income at Pegasus Econometrics Group, said the market had broken out above an older, shallower sloping channel on Friday and was now in an "accelerated channel".

"I find that it's very typical of bond prices...to move within channels and when they're out (of those channels) within accelerated channels," he said. Crosson's near-term objective was slightly above 113, but he expected profit-taking to start appearing in the mid-112 area.
Analysts said recent softness in the Commodity Research Bureau index had been supportive of bonds and that September T-bonds' minor penetration today of Friday's 112-2/32 high was positive.
Gabriel noted that strength in banking stocks was also a positive signal.

Gabriel said a descending one-by-one weekly Gann line from January 1996 highs, now coming in at around 112, and a rising weekly one-by-one line from July 1996 lows, now at around 111, were forming a triangle that largely surrounded the market.

"These two lines are forming a symmetrical triangle that intersects in mid to late July," he said. "It would suggest that...there should be a major move that would develop over the next four weeks as we head toward that resolution."
He predicted that the market would test February's 113-9/32 high fairly soon and might eventually target December 1996 highs in the mid-115s, or possibly higher.
